title: Stock Market Live January 29, 2026: S&P 500 (SPY) Higher on Earnings
summary: The S&P 500 is trading higher on January 29, 2026, driven by mixed corporate earnings reports. Meta Platforms surged 10% after exceeding Q4 estimates and issuing strong Q1 revenue guidance, while Microsoft dropped 7% due to slowing cloud growth and disappointing operating margin guidance. IBM also saw a premarket rise after Bank of America reiterated a buy rating following an earnings beat, dividend declaration, and strong growth across its segments.

title: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust Sees Weekly Outflows Amid Tech Volatility
summary: The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) experienced a 0.35% drop and $9.26 billion in net outflows over the past week, partly due to volatility in its major tech holdings. Nvidia, despite short-term fluctuations, maintains a Strong Buy rating due to strong AI demand, while Apple, heading into Q1 2026 earnings, shows robust iPhone demand and services growth, earning it a Moderate Buy. Microsoft is poised for strong Q2 2026 results, driven by AI and Azure, leading to a Strong Buy rating despite recent valuation concerns.

title: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust Sees Positive Fund Flows
summary: The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ($SPY) has experienced positive fund flows, with a 5-day net inflow of $2.1 billion, partly driven by market sentiment on its largest holdings. Key companies influencing this inflow include Nvidia Corporation due to its AI chip market performance, Apple Inc. despite privacy concerns, and Microsoft, which is actively pursuing AI initiatives with Copilot+. These companies remain strong draws for investors, maintaining positive analyst outlooks despite individual challenges.

title: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust Faces Fund Outflows Amid Market Shifts
summary: The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) experienced a 5-day net outflow of $6.33 billion despite a 1.64% rise in the past week, attributed to market sentiment on its major holdings. Nvidia faces skepticism from investors like Michael Burry due to AI enthusiasm similar to the late 90s tech bubble, contrasting with most analysts' 'Buy' ratings. Apple is navigating potential partnerships with Intel and legal challenges in India, while Microsoft has seen its stock climb after Google withdrew its antitrust complaint in Europe, though regulatory scrutiny on its cloud practices continues.

title: Be Thankful to These ETFs This Year

title: How to invest in the S&P 500 without betting hard on the ‘FAAMG’ stocks that are 20% of the index
summary: This article discusses how to invest in the S&P 500 without heavily relying on the "FAAMG" stocks (Facebook, Apple, Amazon.com, Microsoft, and Google/Alphabet), which represent a significant portion of the index's valuation. It suggests that when investing in a standard S&P 500 index fund, one is implicitly making a large bet on the continued success of these five tech giants. The article hints at an alternative strategy, specifically mentioning an "Equal-weight S&P 500 ETF," for investors looking to diversify away from the concentrated influence of FAAMG stocks within the S&P 500.
